summary: Feed s145_double to NDR is degraded: 9.1% duplicates and 18.6% one-way TCP sessions. NDR requires bidirectional full-payload visibility - one-way breaks session reassembly and detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating overlapping sources (e.g., SPANs from both sides of a link or overlapping TAP/SPAN feeds) without deduplication. Same packet arrives via two paths and is forwarded twice to the NDR, measured as 223/2459 duplicates (9.1% > 5% threshold).
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR wastes CPU/storage on duplicate packets, inflates flow/connection counts, skews analytics and can trigger false positives or missed detections due to reassembly confusion.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication (hash-based, ~10ms window) after aggregation and before delivery to NDR to suppress duplicates while preserving one copy of each packet.

findings.root_cause: Only one direction of TCP sessions is reaching the NDR (29/156 sessions one-way, 18.6%). Most likely SPAN configured for RX-only/TX-only, asymmetric routing with tap only on one path, or packet-broker load-balancing/filter splitting directions across different tool ports instead of aggregating both directions to this NDR.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs_both_directions=true for TCP reassembly, protocol decoding and attack detection. One-way sessions cannot be reassembled, so detection coverage drops, alerts are missed and investigations lack return traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Configure packet broker to aggregate both directions of each flow to the same NDR port. If load-balancing to multiple NDRs, use symmetric 5-tuple flow hashing so forward and reverse of a session go to the same tool; verify SPAN/TAP covers both directions of asymmetric paths.
